## What this is

This document embeds live [CanvasXpress](https://canvasxpress.org) charts directly in
a Quarto HTML page using the `canvasxpress` shortcode. Each chart below is a **real
CanvasXpress instance** — hover for tooltips, drag to zoom, and use the toolbar
(top-right on hover) to export, reconfigure, or reset.

Every chart is defined by a small JSON spec file (the `data` + `config` arguments to
`new CanvasXpress({...})`), so the figures are fully reproducible and version-controllable.

The shortcode syntax is:

``` markdown
{{{< canvasxpress specs/bar.json >}}}
{{{< canvasxpress spec="specs/scatter.json" width="800" height="400" >}}}
```

## Bar chart

A grouped bar chart with a legend, straight from `specs/bar.json`:

{{< canvasxpress specs/bar.json >}}

## Scatter plot

Bubble size encodes a third variable (`hp`). Drag a rectangle to zoom, double-click to
reset:

{{< canvasxpress spec="specs/scatter.json" width="800" height="450" >}}

## Heatmap

A clustered expression heatmap — the dendrograms are computed by CanvasXpress at render
time:

{{< canvasxpress spec="specs/heatmap.json" width="800" height="450" >}}

## Boxplot

Distributions grouped by a categorical factor, colored by group:

{{< canvasxpress specs/boxplot.json >}}

## How it works

1. The extension injects the CanvasXpress CSS + JS into the document `<head>` **once**,
   from the CDN — no manual `<script>` wiring, no local dependencies.
2. Each `{{{< canvasxpress ... >}}}` shortcode reads its JSON spec, stamps a `renderTo`
   target, and constructs one live chart.
3. Only HTML output formats render the charts (other formats emit nothing), since a
   CanvasXpress chart is an interactive `<canvas>`.

To reproduce this page:

``` bash
quarto add neuhausi/canvasxpress-quarto   # once, installs the extension
quarto render demo/demo.qmd --to html
```

See the [extension README](https://github.com/neuhausi/canvasxpress-quarto) for the full
shortcode reference.
